chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ishaq ibn Adam, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Mufaddal ibn Hassan al-Dalani, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, I was in my salat and then remembered in the second rak'ah, while I was in the recitation, that I had not pronounced the iqamah. So what should I do?

He عليه السلام said: "Be silent at the place of your recitation and say: 'Qad qamati al-salat, qad qamati al-salat,' then continue with your recitation and your salat, and your salat has been completed."

key_terms.أُقِمْ: to pronounce the iqamah before beginning salat
key_terms.الرَّكْعَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ: the second unit of the prayer, where the omission was remembered
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the ritual prayer being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةِ: the recitation within the prayer during which the person noticed the omission
key_terms.امْضِ: continue on with the prayer without starting over
key_terms.تَمَّتْ صَلَاتُكَ: your prayer is considered complete and valid
key_terms.قَدْ قَامَتِ الصَّلَاةُ: the phrase of iqamah the Imam عليه السلام instructs to be said

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they remember during salat that they did not say the iqamah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who remembers during salat that he omitted the iqamah. Imam al-Rida عليه السلام instructs him to pause briefly, say 'Qad qamati al-salat' twice, and then continue the recitation and salat without restarting. It indicates leniency and continuity in the performance of salat when this omission is remembered mid-prayer.
